name: MH-60 Seahawk / Jayhawk
summary: Navalised H-60 family: the Navy's MH-60R submarine hunter and MH-60S utility/rescue aircraft, plus the Coast Guard's orange-and-white MH-60T Jayhawk long-range rescue helicopter.

wings: Four-blade main rotor with a powered folding head for shipboard stowage
Weapon/sensor pylons on short stubs on the cabin sides (MH-60R/S)
engines: Two engines side by side on the cabin roof, same layout as the Army H-60
Navy/Coast Guard versions often show a rescue hoist mounted above the cabin door
fuselage: MH-60R and Jayhawk: tailwheel set far forward under the rear cabin, giving a short wheelbase
MH-60S keeps the aft tailwheel and big sliding doors on both sides
Chin FLIR ball, belly radar or weather-radar nose bulge depending on version
Navy gray, or Coast Guard white/orange with a red-orange band
tail: Visible hinge line where the tail pylon folds forward for ship storage
Canted four-blade tail rotor and a low horizontal stabilator like the Army H-60

tellTales: Tailwheel placed far forward under the rear cabin rather than at the end of the tail
Navy gray or Coast Guard orange-and-white with a hoist above the cabin door
Folding hinge visible across the tail pylon

confusedWith.howToTell: The naval H-60s carry a hoist, sensor balls or radar and a folding tail, usually in gray or orange; the MH-60R and Jayhawk also move the tailwheel far forward while the Army Black Hawk's sits at the tail.
The Coast Guard's other orange helicopter, the MH-65 Dolphin, is much smaller, single-cabin, with a shrouded Fenestron tail; the Jayhawk has an open canted tail rotor and is far bigger.
The S-92 is taller and boxier with sponsons for retractable gear and a rear ramp; the MH-60 is long and low with fixed wheels.

usCount.source: USN MH-60R/S ~520 (FlightGlobal World Air Forces 2025) + USCG 48 MH-60T (Defense Daily / USCG 2025)
